extracted.intended_audience: abolitionists and the general American public (mid-19th century)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplars for delivering public anti-slavery speeches and orations that expose the moral, legal, and social evils of slavery and mobilize citizens to action. Emphasizes rhetorical strategies, evidence choices, and moral framing used in mid-19th-century abolitionist addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use indisputable legal evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: I will refer you to the laws adopted by the legislatures of the slave states. I give you such evidence, because it cannot be invalidated nor denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer quoting slave codes and statutory provisions rather than relying solely on personal experience, abolitionist declarations, or isolated newspaper advertisements—because legislative text cannot be easily dismissed as biased or anecdotal. Use such official citations to establish incontrovertible facts about the legal structure of slavery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose national hypocrisy by contrasting rhetoric and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Standing with God and the crushed and bleeding slave on this occasion, I will... denounce, with all the emphasis I can command, everything that serves to perpetuate slavery—the great sin and shame of America!... America is false to the past, false to the present, and solemnly binds herself to be false to the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame arguments by juxtaposing national ideals (Declaration of Independence, patriotism, religion) with concrete practices (slaveholding, fugitive slave laws, slave markets) to reveal moral inconsistency. Use the nation’s own language and symbols to heighten the sense of betrayal and urgency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use scorching irony and harsh rhetoric when moral clarity exists
rubrics_metrics.description: At a time like this, scorching irony, not convincing argument, is needed. Oh! had I the ability... I would to-day pour out a fiery stream of biting ridicule, blasting reproach, withering sarcasm, and stern rebuke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When injustice is plain and self-evident, favor forceful, ironic, and satirical modes of address over measured logical exposition. Employ ridicule, sarcasm, and thunderous denunciation to quicken public feeling and rouse conscience rather than prolonged debate about settled moral facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirm fundamental truths; do not waste time proving the self-evident
rubrics_metrics.description: What point in the anti-slavery creed would you have me argue? ... The manhood of the slave is conceded already. Nobody doubts it. ... For the present, it is enough to affirm the equal manhood of the Negro race.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid arguing points already conceded or self-evident (e.g., that slaves are human or entitled to liberty). Instead, build from acknowledged premises and direct rhetorical energy toward exposing injustice and demanding remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invoke patriotism to demand repentance and reform, not to excuse injustice
rubrics_metrics.description: I would invoke the spirit of patriotism; not in a narrow and restricted sense... not to cover up our national sins, but to inspire us with sincere repentance; not to hide our shame... but utterly to abolish the cause of that shame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reclaim the language of patriotism to call citizens to conscience and corrective action. Use appeals to national honor and divine law to motivate abolitionist change rather than to defend the status quo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid, concrete, and horrific imagery to awaken conscience
rubrics_metrics.description: Hear his savage yells and his blood-chilling oaths... See that girl of thirteen, weeping... The crack you heard was the sound of the slave whip; the scream you heard was from the woman you saw with the babe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ concrete narrative scenes, sensory detail, and vivid anecdotes (drives to market, auctions, lashes, family separations) to make abstract injustices tangible and emotionally compelling to listeners or readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterize slavery as systemic, religiously and morally abhorrent
rubrics_metrics.description: I have shown that slavery is wicked—wicked, in that it violates the great law of liberty... wicked, in that it contravenes the laws of eternal justice, and tramples in the dust all the humane and heavenly precepts of the New Testament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situate slavery as a comprehensive moral evil that contradicts divine law, natural rights, and national ideals. Use theological, ethical, and philosophical arguments to broaden condemnation beyond isolated abuses to systemic sin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose legal and institutional mechanisms thatenable slavery (e.g., Fugitive Slave Law)
rubrics_metrics.description: By an act of the American congress... the power to hold, hunt, and sell men, women, and children as slaves... The fugitive slave law makes MERCY TO THEM A CRIME; and bribes the judge who tries them. An American judge GETS TEN DOLLARS FOR EVERY VICTIM HE CONSIGNS to slavery...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and publicize the statutes, judicial incentives, and federal measures that entrench slavery—show how law and policy nationalize and legitimize oppression. Emphasize procedural unfairness (one-sided hearings, monetary incentives) to undermine claims of lawful justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate northern complicity and the wide moral contagion of slavery
rubrics_metrics.description: The northern people have been long connected with slavery; they have been linked to a decaying corpse... The pestiferous breath of slavery taints the whole moral atmosphere of the north, and enervates the moral energies of the whole people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold northern institutions, parties, churches, and citizens accountable by tracing economic, political, and cultural links to slavery. Show that slavery’s corruption extends beyond the South to implicate the whole nation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warn of consequences and urge timely action
rubrics_metrics.description: I warn the American people... to BEWARE!... the avenging angel may pass over our land, and the sable bondmen now in chains, may become the instruments of our nation’s chastisement!... There is a point beyond which human endurance cannot go.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prophetic warnings about social, political, or divine consequences to create urgency and motivate preventive reform. Frame abolition as necessary to avert national calamity and moral reckoning.
